join_order.description: Filter region to find EUROPE regionkey, then collect nation_keys where n_regionkey matches
join_order.notes: nation_keys fit in tiny bitset/array; scan supplier checking s_nationkey membership

join_order.description: For each qualifying part, use grouped index into partsupp, filter to EUROPE suppliers via supplier lookup index
join_order.probe: partsupp(via grouped index per qualifying part)
join_order.notes: ~8K parts × 4 partsupp rows each = ~32K probes; use supplier_s_suppkey_lookup for O(1) nationkey check

steps.operation: Scan region (5 rows), find r_regionkey where r_name = :r_name_eq. Scan nation (25 rows), collect n_nationkey where n_regionkey matches. Build europe_nation_bitset.
Load supplier_s_suppkey_lookup index. Scan s_nationkey (100K rows), for each supplier check if s_nationkey is in europe_nation_set. Build bitset indexed by suppkey.
steps.output: europe_supplier_bitset sized to max_suppkey (~100K), ~20K bits set

steps.operation: Load p_type dict, find all dict codes where string ends with pattern suffix (e.g. 'BRASS'). Parallel scan part table: check p_size == :p_size_eq AND p_type code in matching_codes set. Collect qualifying partkeys into compact array using two-pass parallel scatter.

Load partsupp_ps_partkey_grouped index. For each qualifying partkey, lookup (start, count) in grouped index. For each partsupp row in [start, start+count), load ps_suppkey, check europe_supplier_bitset. If EUROPE supplier, load ps_supplycost and track MIN. Store min_cost per qualifying part, and the suppkey that achieved it.

For each qualifying part where a valid min_cost was found, the best_suppkey is already known from step above (track both min cost and corresponding suppkey in single pass). Use supplier_s_suppkey_lookup to get supplier row_id. Collect (partkey, part_rowid, supp_rowid, nationkey) tuples.

For each result tuple, load output columns: s_acctbal, s_name (varlen), n_name (varlen from nation), p_partkey, p_mfgr (dict decode), s_address (varlen), s_phone (varlen), s_comment (varlen). Late materialization: only load varlen strings for final results.
Partial sort / top-K selection: ORDER BY s_acctbal DESC, n_name ASC, s_name ASC, p_partkey ASC, LIMIT :limit. Use std::partial_sort with limit=100 on ~8K rows.

data_structures.result_tuples: compact_array(~8000, struct{partkey, part_rowid, supp_rowid, nationkey, min_cost})

parallel_phases.notes: Phase 1: parallel count per thread. Phase 2: prefix-sum + parallel scatter into compact array. Avoids serial merge.
Partition qualifying_partkeys into morsels. Each thread processes its morsels independently — no shared state needed since each part is independent.

indexes.purpose: O(1) lookup of partsupp rows for each qualifying partkey; yields (start, count) pair, exactly 4 rows per part
indexes.layout: uint64_t num_entries, then uint32_t[num_entries*2] interleaved [start, count]

indexes.purpose: O(1) lookup supplier row_id by suppkey for nationkey check and output materialization
indexes.layout: uint64_t num_entries, then int32_t[num_entries] where arr[suppkey] = row_id

advice.partsupp_columns: MADV_RANDOM for indexed access via grouped index
advice.supplier_columns: MADV_SEQUENTIAL for initial nationkey scan, MADV_RANDOM for later lookups

mmap_strategy.raii_scoping: Declare all mmap resources BEFORE RAII timer scope to exclude munmap TLB shootdown cost from timing

key_optimizations: Single-pass min-cost tracking: track both min_cost AND best_suppkey simultaneously to avoid second pass over partsupp
Bitset for EUROPE supplier membership: O(1) check per ps_suppkey, cache-friendly
Compact qualifying arrays sized to ~8K rows, not 2M part keyspace
Late materialization: load varlen strings (s_name, s_address, s_phone, s_comment, n_name) only for final 100 rows after top-K selection
Two-pass parallel scatter for part filtering to avoid serial bottleneck
partial_sort for top-100 on 8K rows instead of full sort
